answer: Pair strangers at random and make them build together: each epoch an agent is matched with partners it did not choose and must co-produce work whose parts only fit if each contributor supplies different input. One operator steering many puppets cannot sit at every table at once — like a zephyr filling a marble hall through one narrow door, its presence thins wherever it spreads. Partners cross-check each other's work, so a copied quill betrays the set, and failed collaborations cost the puppets their standing. Limit: matching must stay fair, or unlucky pairings punish the innocent.
